title: MIT researchers develop self-organizing artificial neural network
excerpt: A study published in PNAS shows that neural networks can build their own learning machinery without developer guidance.
bodyHtml:
Scientists at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research and the K. Lisa Yang Integrative Computational Neuroscience Center published a paper in the journal PNAS on October 9, 2026. The researchers demonstrated that an artificial neural network can build its own learning machinery by organizing itself using simple rules for adjusting connections.

The team created a network of randomly connected units that reshaped itself into an information-processing system. This model uses self-assembling motifs that reorganize through an optimization strategy similar to gradient descent, a method where connections are adjusted in response to errors to improve performance.

The researchers found that this self-organizing network performed at a level similar to networks designed using back-propagation, an algorithm commonly used in modern machine learning. The team suggests that self-organization is a critical starting point for biological plausibility in artificial intelligence research.
topic: How artificial neural networks build their own learning machinery
